why: The financing instrument itself: Component 1 (US$60m) funds last-mile connectivity to 118 city halls, six geographic lots, vulnerable communes prioritised. Only document with quantified municipal ICT targets.
Distinct in-window event: KfW-funded PDiMa announced, 136 municipal buildings stated as all town halls in Togo, plus 1488 schools and 253 health centres.
Distinct in-window completed step: hardware actually delivered to five pilot communes on 8 April 2026. Completed step beats announced intention.

The operative procedures manual of the Ministry of Health: sets the peripheral-level data chain (paper primary tools, RMA/RTA compiled locally, keyed into DHIS2 by the facility or ASC). Primary beats commentary.
Distinct in-window completed step: tele-ultrasound in service at three rural health centres from 9 June 2026, first of twelve beneficiary facilities.
Distinct in-window instrument: IDA additional credit funding Electronic Health Record introduction with EHR availability as a results indicator; establishes EHR is still a reform, not a capability.
The system itself, in the ministry's own words: CIPT/SIPAO commissioned 29 April 2022, workstations deployed in Lome only. Settles both existence and the limit of rural coverage.
Only in-window event placing computer hardware in non-Lome police stations: new commissariats at Mango and Cinkasse equipped under the IOM partnership.

States the operative collection circuit: paper forms at schools forwarded to inspectorates for entry into StatEduc, DHIS2 piloted alongside since 2019 at national scale. English original captured; the /fr/ page is machine-translated.
Distinct in-window ministerial event: national classes digitalisees programme opened 12 September 2025 with a pilot across all seven education regions explicitly including rural schools.
Same file as the digital.localgov selection, chosen here for its distinct payload: 1488 public schools (22% of public schools) to be connected under PDiMa. One file, two selections.
The governing statute: Article 7 gives every rural commune a centre d'etat civil, Article 15 makes registration manuels et/ou informatises with equal legal value. Statute beats news-of-statute.

Distinct in-window completed step: online request service for civil-status act copies launched 19 December 2025 across five pilot communes. File authored by a sibling slice; my duplicate capture of the same URL was withdrawn.
Distinct later event: hardware delivered 8 April 2026 to unblock the pilot. Same file as the digital.localgov selection; one file, two selections.

The supervisory institution itself. The controlling statute (loi 2019-014, Article 27 on solely-automated decisions) is already held in raw/ as DUP-EXACT, so this decree is the admissible baseline: it organises the IPDCP and its inspection, sanction and guidance powers.

Distinct in-window governmental engagement with AI risk: Justice Ministry symposium of 25 November 2025, 50+ state actors, recommending regulation of digital platforms on ethical principles. File authored by a sibling slice; my duplicate capture was withdrawn.
Distinct and most recent in-window event: the data-protection regulator at Togo IGF 2026 setting out compliance obligations and announcing forthcoming sectoral practical guides.

The ministry's own dated statement of the standing position: Novissi cited as an AI use, agricultural AI cited, Data Lab being set up, and a national AI strategy stated as still needed. File authored by a sibling slice; my duplicate capture was withdrawn.

Distinct in-window completed deployment: DMI platform commissioned 12 March 2026, explicitly using AI and real-time data analysis for fraud detection, run from a joint tax/customs/commerce command centre.
Distinct in-window institutional expansion: US$2m Google.org partnership scaling the Togo Data Lab, 27 data specialists across all ministries, 20+ public institutions.

The strongest documentary evidence of ML embedded in a Togolese public information system, co-authored by the minister; carries its own limit that Novissi was a stopgap for the absent social registry and is not evidence of AI in the RSPM.
Distinct in-window event: first Data Infrastructure for Development conference, 19 February 2026, Togo Data Lab under ministry auspices, on AI/ML for geospatial analysis in public service delivery.

Same file as the AI-in-government selection, chosen here for its distinct sectoral payload: ministry projects applying remotely sensed data to agricultural productivity, maritime activity, conservation and climate resilience.

The instrument establishing the public hub network: sub-component 2.1 (US$27m), a regional tech hub near the University of Lome and six satellite innovation pods. Same file as the digital.localgov baseline; one file, two selections.
Distinct in-window completed step: Djanta Tech Hub launched in Lome 7 May 2026 with two programmes, ~72 startups from June 2026 to July 2027 and a Start fund averaging EUR15,000 per project.
Distinct in-window event: six Pods announced for Tone, Kozah, Tchaoudjo, Ogou, Kloto and Zio with an architecture tender closing 30 April 2026 - territorial extension beyond Lome.
